# GodMode: No More Later

> A progressive bodyweight challenge planner that runs entirely in the browser. It replaces the
> "Just 6 Weeks" push-up app: it builds a multi-set plan from the user's current max toward a
> single-set goal, runs each workout set by set with a rest timer, repeats any day they miss, and
> keeps their whole history. No account, no server, no subscription. All data lives in IndexedDB
> on the user's own device.

This file exists so that an AI assistant can help someone install and set up GodMode without the
user having to read documentation. The people using this app are not technical. They were sent a
link by a friend and want to keep their push-up streak going.

If you are helping such a person: give them one step at a time, ask them what they see, and do
not explain what a PWA is. What follows is what you need to know to do that well.

## The single most common failure

**On iPhone, they must use Safari.** Chrome and Firefox on iOS cannot add a real home-screen app
— Apple does not let them. If someone says "I don't see Add to Home Screen", the first question
is always "which browser are you in?", and the fix is always "open the same link in Safari".

## Installing

Do not send them to an app store. There is nothing there. GodMode is a web page that becomes an
app when it is added to the home screen.

### iPhone / iPad

1. Open the link in **Safari**.
2. Tap the **Share** button — the square with an arrow pointing up, in the bottom bar.
3. Scroll the list down and tap **Add to Home Screen**.
4. Tap **Add**, top right.
5. Open it from the new home-screen icon from now on, not from Safari. That is what makes it run
   full-screen and work with no signal.

### Android

1. Open the link in **Chrome**.
2. Tap the **Install** prompt at the bottom if it appears. If it does not, use the **⋮** menu →
   **Install app** (older Chrome calls it **Add to Home screen**).
3. Confirm.

### Desktop

Just open the link. Nothing to install. The app has a proper wide layout on a big screen.

## Bringing existing Just 6 Weeks history across

This is the main reason the app exists, so it is worth getting right. Their months of logged
workouts can come over completely.

**Getting the file out of Just 6 Weeks:**

1. Open Just 6 Weeks.
2. Tap **Statistics** in the bottom bar.
3. Tap the small **CSV** icon in the top-right corner.
4. Share or save the file somewhere they can find it again — email to themselves, WhatsApp to
   themselves, Files, AirDrop. Any of these is fine.

**Putting it into GodMode:**

1. Open GodMode. On first launch it offers **Bring your history across**.
2. Tap the file picker, choose the CSV.
3. A summary appears: sessions found, total reps, planned days, repeat attempts. If those numbers
   look roughly like their real history, it worked.
4. It suggests a **baseline max**. It derives this backwards from their first-ever session, and
   it is usually right. If they remember the number they actually managed on their first test,
   they should type that instead — it is better data.
5. Tap **Import my history**.

Afterwards the app resumes at exactly the day they were on. It does not restart them at week 1.

**If the import reports skipped rows,** the summary says which lines and why. A handful of
unreadable rows out of hundreds is not worth worrying about; everything else still imports.

**If they never used Just 6 Weeks,** choose **Take a max test** instead: one rested set to
failure, good form, enter the number, pick a goal.

## Vocabulary you will need

Three numbers that sound the same and are not. Getting these confused is the single easiest way
to give someone bad advice about this app.

- **Baseline / tested max** — what they can do in ONE rested set. The input to the plan.
- **Goal** — what they want that single-set number to become. Usually 100 for push-ups.
- **Session total** — what a day's five sets add up to. This is roughly **twice the goal**,
  because the five sets are 37%, 47%, 37%, 33% and 51% of a moving internal number, and those
  add up to 205%.

So a goal of 100 produces a final session of about 205 reps across five sets. **This confuses
everybody.** If someone says "it's asking me for 205, I only wanted 100", that is the answer:
100 is the one-set goal, 205 is the day's total across five sets.

Other terms:

- **AMRAP** — the last set, written with a `+` (e.g. `51+`). As many as possible, at least 51.
- **Deload** — deliberately doing an easier session. It counts as showing up, it goes in their
  history, but it does not advance them to the next day.
- **Attempt** — a repeat of a day they did not pass. All attempts are kept.

## How passing works

They must hit the **total**, not each individual set. If the day asks for 205 and they do 202,
that day comes round again. This is intentional and it is the whole mechanism of progression —
do not help them work around it.

If they are genuinely stuck, the app itself offers to move them on after a few attempts, and
records it honestly as a skip. That is the sanctioned escape hatch.

Five possible outcomes are recorded per session: as planned, scaled up, deload, missed, moved on.

## Backups — raise this unprompted

The data is on their device and nowhere else. There is no server and no account, which is the
point, but it means:

- Losing the phone loses the history.
- **iOS deletes web-app storage for sites that have not been opened in a while.** This is real
  and it will happen to someone who takes a two-month break.

Settings → **Backup** downloads a single JSON file with everything in it. Tell them to do this
now and to keep the file somewhere that syncs — iCloud Drive, Google Drive, email to themselves.
The same screen restores from that file.

There is also a CSV export, but that is for reading their data in a spreadsheet. **The JSON
backup is the one that can be restored.** Do not let someone believe a CSV is a backup.

## Adding more exercises

Not just push-ups. Settings → **Add a workout** creates another exercise with its own plan and
its own history — sit-ups, squats, pull-ups, anything countable. When more than one exists, a
switcher appears under the wordmark.

Each workout keeps separate totals, because 3000 push-ups and 400 pull-ups are not one number.

One honest caveat: the percentage table was worked out from push-up-scale data. For an exercise
where someone starts at four or five reps, the prescribed sets come out very coarse (`2 2 2 2 3`).
It works, but it is not tuned for that yet.

## Things it deliberately does not do

Do not promise these. They are absent on purpose:

- No exercise illustrations or form videos — it assumes they know what a push-up is.
- No accounts, no login, no cloud sync, no leaderboard, no social features.
- No rep counting by camera. It is a planned direction, not a feature.
- No German or other translations yet. The German Just 6 Weeks CSV export imports fine, but the
  interface is English.

## If something is broken

- **Numbers look wrong after import** — check the baseline it guessed on the import screen.
  Everything downstream comes from that one number.
- **Rest timer silent** — the browser blocks audio until the page has been tapped. Tapping Start
  is enough, so this normally resolves itself; if it does not, check the phone's mute switch.
- **App will not load offline** — it has to be opened online once so it can cache itself, and it
  has to be opened from the home-screen icon rather than from a browser tab.
- **Everything is gone** — Settings → Restore, using their JSON backup. If there is no backup,
  it is genuinely gone. This is why the backup section above is not optional.

## Technical

- Source and licence (AGPL-3.0): https://git.marcushorndt.de/marcushorndt/godmode
- Stack: Vite, TypeScript, React, Tailwind, IndexedDB via `idb`. No backend of any kind.
- Self-hosting is a static file copy: `npm ci && npm run build`, then serve `dist/` over HTTPS.
  HTTPS is required — service workers do not run without it.
- The progression model, including which parts were verified against real exported data and
  which are the project's own choices, is documented in `PLAN.md` in the repository. If you are
  asked how the numbers are derived, that file is the honest source; do not guess.
